summary: Tenant traffic intermittently diverted from pinned model during canary health probe window
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent diversion of requests away from a tenant-pinned model to a fallback variant during the nightly canary health probe window. Impact: ~3-7% of requests for the tenant observed returning responses from the unpinned variant for ~30-90s intervals, causing subtle output differences and an increase in quality alerts. Environment: prod/us-east, Dedicated cluster (enterprise plan).

Observed behaviour: During the automated canary health probe window (03:00-03:10 UTC), some sessions bound to the tenant's pinned model temporarily route to the canary variant. This occurs without the tenant changing any pins or routes. The issue began on 2026-03-09 after a routine canary rollout for the redwood-open-7b-v2 family.

Expected behaviour: Tenant sessions pinned to a specific model/version should maintain affinity and continue to route to that pinned model except for explicit failover conditions (unhealthy instance, capacity exhaustion, or manual override).

Steps to reproduce (customer): 1) Tenant sends steady requests with session token/tenant header to prod endpoint in us-east. 2) Wait for scheduled canary health probe period. 3) Observe 200 responses signed by fallback model (version mismatch in response metadata) while pin remains configured in tenant settings.

Key logs and traces (sanitized): - edge-proxy: cookie-lease refresh at 03:02:14 from health-probe service, set Path=/, Domain=redwood.ai, SameSite=None
- routing-agent: route-resolve[pinned-token=tenant-abc] -> target=canary-redwood-open-7b-v2-20260309-1 at 03:02:15 (decision reason: probe-priority-preempt=true)
- serving-runtime: kv-cache-miss for session-lease token at 03:02:15
- api-gateway: x-tenant-pin header present in request, value=redwood-open-7b-v2@2026-03-08

Customer impact notes: Output variance triggered quality monitors; customer paused a subset of production traf fic and opened this ticket. No data leakage or model-execution errors observed, only routing divergence and output semantics differences.

Hypotheses so far: 1) Health-probe traffic (internal service) is being prioritized by the canary coordinator and temporarily preempts pin reconciliation for overlapping session tokens. 2) Edge cookie/lease refresh from the health-probe modifies affinity state, causing the edge to consider the session ephemeral and eligible for canary routing. 3) A race between the pin-coherence reconciler and canary weight adjuster leaves a short window where fallback policy (probe-priority-preempt) takes precedence.

Initial investigation steps performed: - Verified tenant pin configuration and pin TTLs remain unchanged. - Pulled routing decision logs and correlation IDs for affected requests (samples attached in comments). - Replayed probe traffic in staging with header mutation reproduces diversion consistently when cookie-lease refresh happens immediately before request. - Checked autoscaler and capacity metrics: no GPU shortage or eviction events during windows. - Reviewed recent canary coordinator PRs — two merged changes adjust probe preemption thresholds (PR referenced above).

Immediate mitigations applied: - Disabled probe-priority-preempt for the affected rollout in us-east (temporary guardrail). - Added conservative pin-coherence backoff to delay canary weight shift until existing session leases reconcile (hotfix patch deployed to canary coordinator).

Next steps: - SRE to run additional long-tail tests for cookie-lease refresh + probe timing across region. - Engineering to instrument pin-reconcile latency metrics and add a metric-level alert. - Rework canary coordinator policy to respect pinned-session affinity until TTL expiry unless explicit unhealthy condition is present. - Customer success to monitor customer quality alerts and confirm reduction in diverted requests.
